titleEn: The Secret History of the Mongols — §§255–256: Chinggis Settles His Sons, and the Tangut Answer
part: §§255–256 — Chinggis Settles His Sons, and the Tangut Answer
about: Chinggis, on the eve of the Sartaul campaign, stops Cha’adai from running Jüchi down; Cha’adai and Jüchi agree to put Ögödei forward; Chinggis lectures his sons on keeping to their words, hears Ögödei and Tolui speak, and issues a decree that a descendant of each of his brothers’ lines shall be put in charge, while Ögödei’s line is promised that no worthless man will be born to it. In §256 he sends to Burqan of the Tangut, who had once offered to be his right hand, and Asha Gambu answers insolently for the Tangut; Chinggis reflects on what going against them would have cost. Grammar to watch: long converb chains (-žu, -žü, -n, -rün), the reflexive -(i)jan/-(i)jen, the conditionals -γ̇asu/-ġesü (Ming 呵), -tü ‘having’, the polite plural imperative -dkün/-dqun, and quotations whose closing marks Shiratori sometimes omits. Several passages are obscure in the glosses; the notes say so.

sentences.i: Then Chinggis Qan said:
sentences.n: Tendēče is tende ‘there’ + the ablative, ‘from there’ (Ming 自那裏), the opening ‘thereupon’. Qān is the short form of qaγan; the house rendering keeps the two apart, ‘Qan’ for Qān and ‘Qahan’ for Qaγan, though both name Chinggis here. Ügülerün is ügüle- ‘say’ + the converb of time -rün (‘saying’), the usual hinge before a speech; the speech itself opens in the next unit (the mark is Shiratori’s, printed at Žüči-ji).

morph.gloss: there, then (from tere 'that'; locative adverb) [自那裏]
Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]
ruler, sovereign, khan (title; the short form beside qaγan) [皇帝]
converb of time: saying, when saying

sentences.i: “Why do you speak so of Jüchi?
sentences.n: Žüči-ji is the name + the accusative -ji (after a vowel); the Ming writes 行, which here reads ‘about, of’. Ta (Ming 您) is the polite plural ‘you’, so the Qan speaks to the sons together, though only Cha’adai answers. Keġemüi is keġe- ‘say’ + present -müi (Ming 說有).

morph.gloss: Jüchi, a son's name [人名 行]
you, plural polite (second-person plural pronoun; stem tan- before case endings) [您]

sentences.t: köġüd-ün min-u aqa Žüči ülü-ü bi.
sentences.l: Sons-of my eldest Jüchi not-(?) is.
sentences.i: Is not Jüchi the eldest of my sons?
sentences.n: Köġüd-ün is köġün + plural -d + genitive -ün, ‘of the sons’, and min-u ‘my’ follows it. Aqa (Ming 長, ‘eldest’) before a name works as an adjective, ‘the eldest, Jüchi’. Bi here is the verb ‘is’, not ‘I’ (Ming 有麽); the question rests on ülü-ü ‘not-?’, where I read -ü as a question particle (the Ming puts its 麽 on bi). Note the pair ülü … bi: a negative question that expects ‘yes’.

morph.gloss: I (first-person singular pronoun; stem min- before case endings) [我的]
elder brother (Ming 長 'eldest' when before a name) [長]
question particle (uncertain; the Ming puts its 麽 on the next word)
to be; bi, a short form 'is, exists' (perhaps from bü-) [有麽]

sentences.t: Qoina tein bu keġedkün" keġen žarliγ bolba.
sentences.l: Later thus do-not say-you" saying, decree became.
sentences.i: Never speak so hereafter,” he said, and issued a decree.
sentences.n: Bu is the prohibitive ‘do not’, here with -dkün, a polite plural imperative (the same ending in ineġeġülüdkün a few units on; its exact value is uncertain). Keġen is the converb that closes the quotation. Žarliγ bolba (Ming 聖旨 做了) is rendered by the house phrase ‘issued a decree’. The closing mark is Shiratori’s, at keġedkün.

sentences.i: At these words Cha’adai sneered and said:
sentences.n: Üge-dür is üge ‘word’ + the dative-locative -dür, ‘in/at the word’; this formula (Ene üge-dür …, ‘at this speech’) opens several speeches in this part and is the cue that a reply follows. Müčilžežü (Ming 哂着, ‘smiling at, sneering’) has a stem müčilže- that I infer from the Ming; the converb is -žü. ‘Sneered’ takes the Ming’s 哂 in its mocking sense, which the context supports.

morph.gloss: to smile, sneer (stem inferred from the Ming 哂 'smile at') [哂着]
converb of time: saying, when saying

sentences.i: “Making no answer of skill to Jüchi, the strong one,
sentences.n: Cha’adai’s speech opens here (the mark is Shiratori’s) and runs to bolu-že" (the end of the unit that names Ögödei’s teaching). Küčütü-ji is küčü ‘strength’ + the possessive -tü ‘having’ (Ming 氣力有的), ‘the strength-having one’, + accusative -ji: this is the recurring -tü ‘having’ type. Which way the sentence turns is uncertain: I take erdem-ün qariγ̇u as ‘an answer of skill’ and ülü ügülen as the negated converb ‘not saying’; Žuči is spelled with u here (Žüči elsewhere).

morph.gloss: Jüchi, a son's name [人名 的]

sentences.i: If one loads what has been killed with the mouth, it will not do,
sentences.n: Two lines of a pair; the sense is a guess from the Ming. Alaγsan is ala- ‘kill’ + the participle -γsan (Ming 殺了的); ačiγ̇asu is a stem ačiγ̇a- that I infer from the Ming 䭾 ‘load on a pack-animal’, + conditional -γ̇asu (Ming 呵, ‘if’); boli (Ming 中) ‘will do’. It reads like a proverb, that no corpse is left of a man killed by talk, so there is nothing to load; I give it only as a reading.

morph.gloss: past participle: killed, what has been killed
to load on a pack-animal (stem inferred from the Ming 䭾 'load') [䭾呵]
will do, be acceptable (Ming 中; form uncertain) [中]

sentences.i: and if one flays one put to death by words, it will not do.
sentences.n: The partner of the line before: ama-γ̇ar ‘with the mouth’ there, üge-ġer ‘with words’ here (instrumental -γ̇ar after back vowels, -ġer after front vowels: vowel harmony in the case ending). Üküġülügsen (Ming 死了的) I split as ükü- ‘die’ + an ending of uncertain force + the participle -sen; übčiġesü is a stem übči- (Ming 剝 ‘peel’) + -ġesü, the front-vowel conditional (back-vowel -γ̇asu in the unit before).

morph.gloss: ending of uncertain force (perhaps causative -ġül- plus -g-; the Ming reads plain 'dead')
to flay, strip off the hide (stem inferred from the Ming 剝 'peel') [剝呵]
will do, be acceptable (Ming 中; form uncertain) [中]

sentences.t: Köġüd-ün aqa Žüči ba qojar bi-že.
sentences.l: Sons-of eldest Jüchi we two are-indeed.
sentences.i: Jüchi, the eldest of the sons, and I — we two are here.
sentences.n: Ba qojar is ‘we two’ (Ming 俺 兩箇), the pair being Jüchi and the speaker. Bi-že is the verb ‘be’ (stem bi-) + the assertion particle -že, ‘indeed’ (Ming 有也者).

morph.gloss: elder brother (Ming 長 'eldest' when before a name) [長]
we (first-person plural pronoun; the Ming 俺 'we, excluding you') [俺]
two (follows the pair it counts) [兩箇]

sentences.i: Side by side, let us give our strength to Father Qan.
sentences.n: Ečige-de is the dative-locative (front-vowel -de); the Ming 行 marks the receiver, ‘to’. Qolbaran (Ming 並行) has a stem qolbara- that I infer, ‘to join, go side by side’. Ögsü is ög- ‘give’ + the optative -sü (Ming 與我, ‘let me give’); the plural subject comes from the ‘we two’ before it, hence ‘let us’.

morph.gloss: ruler, sovereign, khan (title; the short form beside qaγan) [皇帝]
to join, go side by side (stem inferred from the Ming 並) [並行]
strength, power (printed küčün, with a stem-final -n; unmarked object of ögsü) [氣力]

sentences.i: Whoever hides, let us cleave him apart together,
sentences.n: The reflexive-possessive -(i)jan (‘one’s own’) is the first of several; here it sits on a participle, so ‘our own man who hides’, with the (i) as Shiratori’s accusative. Daldariγsan(i)-jan is a stem daldari- (Ming 躱避, ‘hide’) I infer + the participle -γsan. Čabčildusu is čabči- ‘hew’ + -ldu- ‘together’ + optative (Ming 共砍, ‘cut together’).

morph.gloss: to hide, take cover (stem inferred from the Ming 躱避) [躱避的自的行]
cleaving, splitting open (Ming 劈開; form uncertain, perhaps a converb) [劈開]
to chop, hew (stem inferred from the Ming 砍) [共砍]

sentences.i: and whoever lags behind, let us sever his heel and hew together.
sentences.n: Again two reflexive-possessives in -jan, one on the participle qožidaγsan(i)- ‘the one who lags’ (Ming 落後了的) and one on borbin(i)- ‘heel’ (Ming 腳後根). The reflexive points back at the subject, so strictly ‘our own laggard, his heel’; the clause as a whole is a warning to their own men, as I read it.

morph.gloss: to lag behind (stem inferred from the Ming 落後) [落後了的 自的行]
heel (Ming 腳後根; printed borbin) [腳後根 自的行]
cutting across, severing (Ming 橫斷 'cut crosswise'; form uncertain) [橫斷]
to chop, hew (stem inferred from the Ming 砍) [共砍]

sentences.i: Ögödei, for his part, is gentle.
sentences.n: Lü (Ming 但, ‘only, but’) I take as a particle of emphasis that sets Ögödei beside the two elder brothers; its force is uncertain. Örüg is ‘peace, calm’ in the glossary, but the Ming here glosses it 敦厚 ‘honest, generous’, said of a person, hence ‘gentle’. Bi again is ‘is’.

morph.gloss: particle 'only, just, for his part' (Ming 但; uncertain) [但]
peace, calm; here the Ming 敦厚 'honest, generous', of a person [敦厚]
to be; bi, a short form 'is, exists' (perhaps from bü-) [有]

sentences.i: Let us put forward Ögödei together:
sentences.n: Keġeldüje is keġe- ‘say’ + -ldu- ‘together’ + the hortative -je (Ming 共說咱, ‘let us say together’). ‘Put forward’ is my reading: Ögödei is the object of ‘say’ and what follows is what is said of him. The plain meaning is ‘let us speak of/to Ögödei’.

morph.gloss: Ögödei, a man's name [人名 行]

sentences.t: Ögödei Qān ečige-jin dergede ažu baraγ̇a jeke maqalai-jin balija taniγ̇uluγ̇asu bolu-že" keġebe.
sentences.l: Ögödei, Qan father-of near staying, shape great fur-cap-of teaching, if-made-to-know, let-it-be" said.
sentences.i: Let Ögödei stay beside his father the Qan, and if he is taught the bearing and the instruction of the great fur cap, so be it,” he said.
sentences.n: A converb chain: ažu ‘staying’ leads to taniγ̇uluγ̇asu ‘if made to know’ (tani- + causative -γ̇ul- + conditional -γ̇asu) and the verb bolu-že ‘so be it’ (bol- + -u + -že). The middle is obscure: baraγ̇a (Ming 形影 ‘shape and shadow’) I render ‘bearing’, and ‘the great fur cap’ (maqalai-jin, Ming 皮帽) I take as a figure for the office; balija (Ming 敎訓) is ‘teaching’. The quotation (Cha’adai’s) closes here, on the mark at bolu-že; the last word is the speaker’s tag keġebe ‘said’.

morph.gloss: ruler, sovereign, khan (title; the short form beside qaγan) [皇帝]
near, beside (Ming 根前; stem uncertain) [根前]
shape, shadow, bearing (Ming 形影; sense uncertain) [形影]
fur cap (Ming 皮帽) [皮帽 的]
teaching, instruction (Ming 敎訓; form uncertain) [敎訓]
assertion particle: indeed, so be it

sentences.i: At these words Chinggis Qahan said:
sentences.n: The same ene üge-dür formula as before (Cha’adai’s speech was introduced the same way), now introducing the reply. Čiṅgis Qaγan, where the Qān of the first unit was the short form.

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]
converb of time: saying, when saying

sentences.i: “What does Jüchi say? Speak your own mind,” he said.
sentences.n: Žüči jaγ̇u keġemü is in the third person (‘what does Jüchi say?’) and then turns to the man himself. Kele-ġen is kele- ‘speak’ + the reflexive -ġen (Ming 說(自的行)); the Ming’s bracket suggests ‘his own’, so ‘speak your own’ is a reading, not certain. The quotation is closed by Shiratori’s mark at kele-ġen".

morph.gloss: reflexive-possessive: one's own (Ming 自的行; reading uncertain)

sentences.i: Jüchi said: “Cha’adai, for his part, has spoken.
sentences.n: A short reply that picks up Cha’adai’s lü ‘for his part’ (as in the unit about Ögödei). Ügülerün … ügülebe: the same verb as converb and as past tense (-be). The quotation opens at Čaγ̇adai (Shiratori’s mark) and runs on to keġeldüje" two units on, so there is no closing mark yet.

morph.gloss: converb of time: saying, when saying
particle 'only, just, for his part' (Ming 但; uncertain) [但]

sentences.t: Čaγ̇adai ba qojar qolbaγ̇aran küčü ögsü.
sentences.l: Cha’adai we two side-by-side strength let-me-give.
sentences.i: Cha’adai and I, we two, will give our strength side by side.
sentences.n: Ba qojar ‘we two’ again, here with Cha’adai the second of the pair. Qolbaγ̇aran (Ming 並行) is the converb of an inferred qolbaγ̇ara-; küčü ‘strength’ is the bare form (Cha’adai’s speech had küčün); ögsü is the optative ‘let me give’.

morph.gloss: we (first-person plural pronoun; the Ming 俺 'we, excluding you') [俺]
two (follows the pair it counts) [兩箇]
to join, go side by side (stem inferred from the Ming 並) [並行]

sentences.i: Let us put forward Ögödei together,” he said.
sentences.n: The quotation of Jüchi closes at keġeldüje"; keġebe is ‘said’. See the earlier unit for my reading of keġeldüje as ‘put forward’.

morph.gloss: Ögödei, a man's name [人名 行]

sentences.i: Chinggis Qahan then issued a decree:
sentences.n: Žarliγ bolurun is bol- + the converb of time -urun, ‘when making a decree’, rendered by the house phrase ‘issued a decree’. The decree runs to ta" (the long speech that follows).

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]

sentences.i: “Why stay joined, side by side?
sentences.n: Qolbaγ̇aratala is qolbaγ̇ara- ‘go side by side’ + -tala ‘until, while’ (Ming 並行); jaγ̇un bi is ‘what is?’. The rhetorical sense is my reading from what follows (the land is wide, so why stand shoulder to shoulder), not a certainty. The decree’s opening mark is Shiratori’s, on Qolbaγ̇aratala.

morph.gloss: to join, go side by side (stem inferred from the Ming 並) [並行]
to be; bi, a short form 'is, exists' (perhaps from bü-) [有]

sentences.i: Mother Etügen is wide.
sentences.n: Ötögen eke is Mother Etügen, the Earth (Ming 地 ‘land’); the printed spelling is Ötögen. Aγ̇ui ‘wide’ (Ming 寬) and bi ‘is’.

morph.gloss: Etügen, the Earth (Ming 地 'land'; the earth-mother's name) [地]
to be; bi, a short form 'is, exists' (perhaps from bü-) [有]

sentences.i: Rivers and waters are many.
sentences.n: Müred and usud are müren ‘river’ and usun ‘water’ with the plural -d, the Ming marking the plural in 每. Olon bi ‘many are’.

morph.gloss: to be; bi, a short form 'is, exists' (perhaps from bü-) [有]

sentences.t: Salqu situ nutuγ aγ̇udkin qari daruγ̇ulun salγaja keġeġed,
sentences.l: Dividing like, camping-ground widening, tribes subduing, let-me-divide, having-said,
sentences.i: Saying, ‘Let me divide them, as one divides, widening your camping-grounds and subduing the tribes,’
sentences.n: A converb chain, daruγ̇ulun (daru- ‘press down’ + causative -γ̇ul- + -n) leading to salγaja ‘let me divide’ (salγa- + hortative -ja, Ming 分咱) and keġeġed ‘having said’. Aγ̇udkin (Ming 敎寬) has a stem aγ̇ud- that I infer from aγ̇ui ‘wide’ and an ending -kin I cannot name. Salqu situ is ‘dividing-like’ (Ming 分的般). Whom Chinggis divided is not stated; the sense is the division of the realm among the sons, which keġeġed makes a quotation within the speech, so I set it in single quotes in `i`.

morph.gloss: like, as (Ming 般; compare metü) [般]
to widen (stem inferred from aγ̇ui 'wide' and the Ming 敎寬 'cause to be wide') [敎寬]
hortative: let me, let us (Ming 咱)

sentences.t: Žüči Čaγ̇adai qojar üges- tür(i)-jen kürülčedkün.
sentences.i: you two, Jüchi and Cha’adai, hold to your own words together.
sentences.n: Üges-tür(i)-jen is üge + plural -s + dative-locative -tür + Shiratori’s (i) + the reflexive -jen, ‘in one’s own words’; the (i) is an unexplained filler. Kürülčedkün is kürü- ‘reach’ + -lče- ‘together’ + the polite plural -dkün (Ming 敎共到您). ‘Hold to’ is my reading of ‘reach’, supported by kürkü-jin tula ‘because of not reaching [their words]’ some units on.

morph.gloss: two (follows the pair it counts) [兩箇]
to reach, hold to [敎共到您]

sentences.i: Do not make the people laugh at you.
sentences.n: Ineġeġülüdkün is ineġe- ‘laugh’ + causative -ġül- + -dkün, with bu ‘do not’ (the same bu … -dkün as in the first unit of the part). Irgen-e carries the Ming 行, ‘at, to’.

sentences.i: Do not make the common people howl with laughter.
sentences.n: Qabqariγ̇uludqun has a stem qabqari- ‘laugh heartily’ inferred from the Ming 大咲 ‘laugh loudly’, + causative + -dqun, the back-vowel form of the ending in -dkün. Haran-a (haran ‘common people’ + dative -a, back-vowel harmony) answers irgen-e in the unit before.

morph.gloss: to laugh loudly (stem inferred from the Ming 大咲) [敎大咲您]

sentences.t: Erte Altan, Qučar qojar ene metü üge baraldužu
sentences.l: Formerly Altan, Quchar the two, this like word having-agreed,
sentences.i: Formerly Altan and Quchar, the two, had agreed on a word like this,
sentences.n: Baraldužu is baraldu- ‘settle together’ (a stem I infer from the Ming 議定) + the converb -žu. Metü ‘like’ follows ene ‘this’. Altan and Quchar are the two men whose fate the next lines hint at; Altan is capitalised in Shiratori’s print.

morph.gloss: gold, golden (also a man's name) [人名]
two (follows the pair it counts) [兩箇]
to settle together, agree (stem inferred from the Ming 議定) [議定了着]

sentences.t: žiči üges- tür(i)-jen ülü kürkü-jin tula ker kigdelüġei.
sentences.l: But words-in-own not reaching-of because-of how were-done?
sentences.i: but, because they did not keep to their own words, what was done to them?
sentences.n: The negated participle ülü kürkü-jin tula (kürü- ‘reach’ + -kü + genitive -jin; tula ‘because of’, Ming 上頭) gives the cause. Kigdelüġei is ki- ‘do’ + passive -gde- + past -lüġei (Ming 被做來, ‘was done’): ‘how was it done to them’, a rhetorical question that implies their end without saying it. Žiči ‘but, yet’ (Ming 郤).

morph.gloss: because of, on account of (postposition) [上頭]
past: was, were (front-vowel form; Ming 來)

sentences.i: What became of them?
sentences.n: Ambar (Ming 甚麽) is a word known nowhere else; the sense ‘what’ is the Ming’s. Bolγaγdaluγ̇ai is bol- + causative -γa- + passive -γda- + past -luγ̇ai (Ming 被做了來), the back-vowel form of the -lüġei of the unit before: ‘was made to become’.

morph.gloss: what, something (Ming 甚麽; sense uncertain) [怎]
past: was, were (back-vowel form; Ming 了來)

sentences.t: Edöġe Altan, Qučar, qojar-un uruγ̇ud-ača tan-luγ̇a salγalduja.
sentences.l: Now Altan, Quchar the-two-of descendants-from you-with let-us-divide.
sentences.i: Now let us part, together with you, from the descendants of Altan and Quchar.
sentences.n: Uruγ̇ud-ača is ‘from the descendants’ (uruγ + plural -ud + ablative -ača). Salγalduja is salγa- ‘divide’ + -ldu- + hortative -ja (Ming 敎分咱, ‘let us divide’), and tan-luγ̇a is ‘with you’ (the stem tan- of ta + comitative). Whom this sets apart from whom is uncertain: I read ‘let us separate ourselves (you and me) from them’, but ‘let us divide you off from them’ is just as possible.

morph.gloss: gold, golden (also a man's name) [人名]
you (plural, polite; oblique stem tan-) [您 一同]

sentences.t: Teden-i üžežü jaγ̇u osoldaqun ta" keġeġed
sentences.i: Seeing them, how could you be remiss?” he said,
sentences.n: Teden-i is ‘those’ with the accusative; üžežü is üže- ‘see’ + converb -žü. Osoldaqun is a stem osolda- (Ming 怠慢, ‘be negligent’) + an ending -qun that I take as the polite plural; jaγ̇u is ‘what’ used as ‘how’. The decree ends at ta" and keġeġed (‘having said’) is the speaker’s tag.

morph.gloss: to be negligent, remiss (stem inferred from the Ming 怠慢) [怠慢了]
you, plural polite (second-person plural pronoun; stem tan- before case endings) [您]

sentences.i: “What does Ögödei say? Speak!” he said.
sentences.n: Same pattern as Jüchi’s turn: the name with jaγ̇u keġemü ‘what does he say?’, then the imperative kelele (kele- ‘speak’ + -le, Ming 說). Shiratori prints the closing mark after Kelele but no opening; I supply the opening in `i`.

sentences.t: Ögödei ügülerün: "Qaγan-eče sojurγažu ügüle keġegdeġesü jaγ̇u-ban ügülekü bi.
sentences.l: Ögödei saying: "Qaγan-from favour-showing speak, if-being-told, what-own to-speak I.
sentences.i: Ögödei said: “If the Qahan, showing favour, tells me ‘Speak,’ what shall I say of my own?
sentences.n: Qaγan-eče is the ablative -eče, ‘from the Qahan’; the Ming has (自) for the ablative. Keġegdeġesü is keġe- ‘say’ + passive -gde- + conditional -ġesü: ‘if it is said (to me)’, with ügüle ‘speak!’ as the quoted command. Jaγ̇u-ban is ‘what’ + the reflexive -ban (Ming 甚麽自的行) before the participle ügülekü. Ögödei’s speech opens at Qaγan-eče (Shiratori’s mark).

morph.gloss: converb of time: saying, when saying
to show favour, bestow grace [恩賜着]
to speak, to say (the bare stem, used as imperative) [說]
I (first-person singular pronoun; stems na-, nama-, min- before case endings) [我]

sentences.i: Saying I cannot, how am I to speak?
sentences.n: Ülü čidaqu is ülü ‘not’ + the participle čida- ‘be able’ + -qu (Ming 能). Keġen closes the thought, and ker ügülekü ‘how to speak’ asks the question. Ülü, not ese, since the verb is a participle of present or future (the ese / ülü contrast recurs later in this part).

sentences.i: As far as I am able, I will take care — so I say.
sentences.n: Čidaqui-bar is the participle + the instrumental -bar, ‘by what one can do’ (Ming 依着). Qataγ̇učisuγai (Ming 謹愼我) is a stem qataγ̇uči- I infer + the optative -suγai, ‘let me’. Kü (Ming 也) is a particle of emphasis, and keġemü-že ‘says indeed’ closes with the assertion -že.

morph.gloss: to be able, can [能的 依着]
to be careful, take care (stem inferred from the Ming 謹愼) [謹︀愼我]

sentences.t: Mönö qoina maqa uruγ-tur min-u olaṅ-dur qučiγ̇asu hüker-e ülü idegdekü
sentences.l: Long after perhaps descendants-among my green-grass-in, if-wrapped, ox-by not to-be-eaten.
sentences.i: In the long time to come, it may be that one of my descendants, wrapped in green grass, will not be eaten by the ox;
sentences.n: A conditional pair. Qučiγ̇asu is a stem qučiγ̇a- ‘wrap up’ (Ming 包褁) + the conditional -γ̇asu ‘if’; idegdekü is ide- ‘eat’ + passive -gde- + participle -kü, ‘to be eaten’, and hüker-e is the doer of the passive in the dative (‘by the ox’). Mönö qoina (Ming 久 後) is ‘long hereafter’, and maqa (Ming 莫) ‘perhaps’. Min-u ‘my’ stands after uruγ-tur ‘among descendants’ in the print (the word order is odd; compare min-u uruγ-tur later).

morph.gloss: long, for long (Ming 久; with qoina 'long hereafter') [久]
perhaps (Ming 莫 'lest', in a doubtful sense) [莫]
I (first-person singular pronoun; stem min- before case endings) [我的]
green grass (Ming 靑草) [靑草 裏]
to wrap up (stem inferred from the Ming 包褁) [包褁呵]
dative-locative: by, to (the Ming 行; names the doer of a passive)

sentences.i: wrapped in fat, he will not be eaten by the dog;
sentences.n: The second half of the pair: eġükün-dür ‘in fat’ (dative-locative, front-vowel -dür) answers olaṅ-dur ‘in green grass’ (back-vowel -dur) of the unit before, and noγaj-a is ‘by the dog’ (j a glide). The pair says that such a man is fit for neither beast to eat — a way of calling him worthless — but the Ming gives only the grammar, so the figure is my reading.

morph.gloss: fat, grease (Ming 脂膏) [脂膏 裏]
to wrap up (stem inferred from the Ming 包褁) [包褁呵]
dative-locative: by, to (j is a glide; the Ming 行)

sentences.t: töreġešü qandaγai ketüs quluγana söles aldaquj-uγ̇u.
sentences.l: If-born, the-qandaγai crossing, the-mouse following, will-he-not-fail?
sentences.i: if one is born who steps across the qandaγai and follows the mouse, will he not go astray?
sentences.n: A passage I give only as a reading. Qandaγai is Ming 獸名 ‘beast’, not further identified; ketüs (Ming 橫越着 ‘crossing’) and söles (Ming 順應着 ‘following’) are converbs in -s from stems I infer; aldaquj-uγ̇u is alda- ‘err’ + -qu + a question particle -uγ̇u (Ming 不中麽). The sense, ‘passes over the great game and chases the mouse’, is a guess at the figure.

morph.gloss: an animal (Ming 獸名 'beast name'; not further identified) [獸名]
to cross over (stem inferred from the Ming) [橫越着]
to follow, comply with (stem inferred from the Ming 順應) [順應着]

sentences.i: These things only do I say.
sentences.n: Edül-jüġen-že is edül ‘these’ (Ming 這些; an odd form) + the reflexive -jüġen + -že (Ming 但, ‘only’). Keġemü ‘says’ in the first person, as Mongol allows.

morph.gloss: these (Ming 這些; ede + -l, uncertain) [這些自的行但]

sentences.i: What else should I say?” he said.
sentences.n: Busu ‘other’ (Ming 別) before jaγ̇u ‘what’. Ögödei’s speech closes at bi".

morph.gloss: I (first-person singular pronoun; stems na-, nama-, min- before case endings) [我]

sentences.t: Ene üge-dür Čiṅgis Qaγan žarliγ bolurun:
sentences.l: This word-in Chinggis Qaγan decree when-becoming:
sentences.i: At these words Chinggis Qahan issued a decree:
sentences.n: The ene üge-dür formula and žarliγ bolurun once more; a new decree begins in the next unit.

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]

sentences.t: "Öġödei eimün üges ügülekü böġesü bolu-že" keġebe.
sentences.l: "Ögödei, such words to-speak if-it-be, let-it-be" said.
sentences.i: “Ögödei, if you say such words, so be it,” he said.
sentences.n: Böġesü is bü- ‘be’ + the conditional -ġesü (Ming 有呵), ‘if it is (the case that)’; ügülekü is the participle ‘to speak’, so ‘if it is to be spoken’. Bolu-že ‘so be it’ again. Öġödei is spelled thus here against Ögödei elsewhere. The decree opens at Öġödei (Shiratori’s mark).

morph.gloss: Ögödei, a man's name (printed Öġödei) [人名]
such, of this kind (Ming 這般每) [這般每]
assertion particle: indeed, so be it

sentences.t: Basa Tolui jaγ̇u keġemü. Kelele" keġebe.
sentences.l: Again Tolui what says. Speak" said.
sentences.i: Next: “What does Tolui say? Speak!” he said.
sentences.n: Basa (Ming 再) ‘again’. Same formula as for Jüchi and Ögödei. Shiratori prints a closing mark after Kelele but no opening; I supply it in `i`.

sentences.t: Tolui ügülerün: "Bi Qaγan ečige-jin nereidügsen aqa-juγ̇an dergede ažu
sentences.l: Tolui saying: "I, Qaγan father-of named elder-brother-own near staying,
sentences.i: Tolui said: “I, staying beside my elder brother, the one Father Qahan named,
sentences.n: Tolui’s long speech is a single converb chain, ažu … duradγažu … seriġülžü … bolžu … čaγ̇uražu … bolγažu, which ends in ögsü (‘let me give’) at the close of the speech. The opening is Shiratori’s mark at Bi. Nereidügsen aqa-juγ̇an is nereidü- ‘name, mention by name’ + the participle -gsen, + aqa ‘elder brother’ + the reflexive -juγ̇an (Ming 兄自的): the elder brother his father has named, i.e. the heir.

morph.gloss: converb of time: saying, when saying
I (first-person singular pronoun; stems na-, nama-, min- before case endings) [我]
to name, mention by name [名提了的]
reflexive-possessive: one's own (back-vowel form, after a vowel)
near, beside (Ming 根前; stem uncertain) [根前]

sentences.i: reminding him of what he has forgotten and rousing him from sleep,
sentences.n: Umartaγsan-i and umtaraγsan-i are participles in -γsan with the accusative -i (Ming 行), objects of the converbs duradγažu ‘recalling’ and seriġülžü (seri- ‘wake’ + causative -ġül- + -žü) ‘rousing’. The stem umtara- (Ming 睡着了的) I infer.

morph.gloss: to fall asleep (stem inferred from the Ming 睡) [睡着了的 行]

sentences.i: being a companion of assent, a whip for his bay horse,
sentences.n: Že-jin is že ‘assent, ‘yes’’ (Ming 應許) + the genitive -jin; a ‘companion of assent’ is one who answers ‘yes’. Žeġerde-jin minaγ̇a is ‘the whip of the bay horse’ (Ming 赤馬的鞭子), i.e. one who keeps his master’s horse going. Note this že is not the že ‘nephew’ of the glossary (Ming 外甥): the Ming here is 應許.

sentences.t: že-dēče ülü qožidan žerge-dēče ülü solaitan
sentences.l: Assent-from not lagging, rank-from not leaving-a-gap,
sentences.i: never lagging behind in assent, never leaving a gap in the line,
sentences.n: Že-dēče and žerge-dēče carry the ablative -dēče with a long vowel (‘from the assent’, ‘from the rank’, Ming 行, 裏). Qožidan and solaitan are converbs in -n from stems qožida- ‘lag behind’ (Ming 落後) and solaita- (Ming 空缺 ‘vacancy’, inferred). Ülü, as the negative of a converb.

morph.gloss: to lag behind (stem inferred from the Ming 落後) [落後]
rank, row, line (Ming 次序) [次序 行]
to leave a gap (stem inferred from the Ming 空缺 'vacancy') [空缺]

sentences.t: urtu čaγ̇ur čaγ̇uražu oqor bolγa bolγažu ögsü.
sentences.l: Long march marching, short fight fighting, let-me-give.
sentences.i: marching on the long march and fighting the short fight, let me give.
sentences.n: Urtu čaγ̇ur čaγ̇uražu ‘long campaign, going on campaign’ pairs a noun with its converb, as in §254; so does oqor bolγa bolγažu (Ming 短厮殺厮殺着, ‘short fight, fighting’), where bolγa- ‘fight’ has the Ming 厮殺. Ögsü ‘let me give’ has no object stated (compare küčün ögsü ‘give strength’ above). Shiratori prints no closing mark after ögsü; the quotation ends there, and I supply the mark in `i`.

morph.gloss: to go out on campaign [征進着]
fight, skirmish (Ming 厮殺 'fight'; perhaps from bol- + -γa-) [厮殺︀]
to fight, skirmish (Ming 厮殺) [厮殺︀着]

sentences.t: keġen ügüleġesü Čiṅgis Qaγan žöbšijen žarliγ bolurun:
sentences.l: Saying, if-speaking, Chinggis Qaγan agreeing decree when-becoming:
sentences.i: When he had said this, Chinggis Qahan agreed and issued a decree:
sentences.n: Ügüleġesü is ügüle- + the conditional -ġesü (Ming 說呵), ‘when he had spoken’. Žöbšijen (Ming 道是 ‘say it is so’) has a stem žöbši- ‘approve’ that I infer; its ending -jen is uncertain. Žarliγ bolurun as before.

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]
to approve, assent (Ming 道是 'say it is so') [道是]

sentences.i: “From Qasar’s descendants, let one — their own — be put in charge.
sentences.n: Four units of one pattern, one each for the lines of Qasar, Alchidai, Ödchigin and Belgütei. Medeġül is mede- ‘know, manage’ + causative -ġül (Ming 敎管 ‘have managed’), the bare stem standing as imperative; the reflexive -jen on nigen(i) (‘one’) I leave as ‘their own’. What the one is to be in charge of the Ming does not say. The decree opens at Qasar-un (Shiratori’s mark).

morph.gloss: causative: have (it) managed (bare stem used as imperative; uncertain)

sentences.i: From Alchidai’s descendants, let one — their own — be put in charge.
sentences.n: As above; Alčidai-jin takes the genitive -jin after a vowel.

morph.gloss: causative: have (it) managed (bare stem used as imperative; uncertain)

sentences.i: From Ödchigin’s descendants, let one — their own — be put in charge.
sentences.n: As above. The genitive is printed -(n)ü after a front-vowel name Ödčigin-.

morph.gloss: Ödchigin, a man's name [人名 的]
causative: have (it) managed (bare stem used as imperative; uncertain)

sentences.i: From Belgütei’s descendants, let one — their own — be put in charge.
sentences.n: As above; -jin again after a vowel.

morph.gloss: Belgütei, the younger brother of Chinggis [人名 的]
causative: have (it) managed (bare stem used as imperative; uncertain)

sentences.t: Tein sedkižü min-u urug-i nigen-i medeġülžü
sentences.l: Thus thinking, my descendants-(acc) one-(acc) putting-in-charge,
sentences.i: Thinking so, and having one of my descendants put in charge,
sentences.n: Sedkižü is sedki- ‘think’ + converb -žü; medeġülžü is mede- + causative -ġül- + -žü, ‘putting in charge’ (Ming 敎管着). Urug-i and nigen-i are ‘descendants’ and ‘one’, both accusative (Ming 行). Who is to be in charge and of what is not stated; this unit and the four before form one arrangement.

morph.gloss: I (first-person singular pronoun; stem min- before case endings) [我的]

sentences.t: min-u žarliγ busu ülü bolγan ese hutaruγ̇asu
sentences.l: My decree other not making, not destroying-if,
sentences.i: if you do not make my decree something else and do not destroy it,
sentences.n: Ese (Ming 不, ‘not (done)’) with a conditional, against ülü with the converb bolγan: bolγan is bol- + causative -γa- + -n, ‘making’ (Ming 做). The ese / ülü contrast: ülü negates a converb or a future, ese negates what has not been done. Hutaruγ̇asu is hutaru- ‘destroy’ (stem inferred from the Ming 毀) + conditional -γ̇asu.

morph.gloss: I (first-person singular pronoun; stem min- before case endings) [我的]
not (negates a past action; ülü negates present or future) [不]
to destroy, ruin (stem inferred from the Ming 毀) [毀了呵]

sentences.i: you will not go wrong, you will not fail.
sentences.n: Endedkün (Ming 差了您) is a stem ende- ‘go wrong’ I infer + the polite plural -dkün; aldaqun-ta is alda- ‘err, fail’ + an ending + ta ‘you’ (Ming 失了您). Both are negated by ülü and read as consequences of the conditional before.

morph.gloss: to go wrong, err (stem inferred from the Ming 差) [差了您]

sentences.t: Ogödei-jin urug-i olaṅ-dur qučiγ̇asu hüker-e ülü idegdekü.
sentences.l: Ögödei-of descendants-(acc) green-grass-in, if-wrapped, ox-by not to-be-eaten.
sentences.i: Wrapped in green grass, the descendants of Ögödei will not be eaten by the ox,
sentences.n: Ögödei’s line (spelled Ogödei- in the print). This repeats Ögödei’s own figure from his speech earlier in this §, now in the Qan’s mouth and with Ögödei’s line as its subject: ‘wrapped in grass, not eaten by the ox’. The Ming gives the same words as in Ögödei’s speech; the sense of the figure is the same uncertain one.

morph.gloss: Ögödei, a man's name (printed Ogödei) [人名的]
green grass (Ming 靑草) [靑草 裏]
to wrap up (stem inferred from the Ming 包褁) [包褁呵]
dative-locative: by, to (the Ming 行; names the doer of a passive)

sentences.i: wrapped in fat, they will not be eaten by the dog;
sentences.n: Second half of the pair; Öġükün-dür is printed with an initial Ö where Ögödei’s speech had Eġükün-dür (same word, Ming 脂膏 ‘fat’).

morph.gloss: fat, grease (Ming 脂膏; printed öġükün) [脂膏 裏]
to wrap up (stem inferred from the Ming 包褁) [包褁呵]
dative-locative: by, to (j is a glide; the Ming 行)

sentences.t: töreġešü min-u uruγ-tur nigen-üġü sain ülü törekü ažuγ̇u"
sentences.l: If-born my descendants-among one-(also) good not to-be-born was"
sentences.i: if they are born, will not even one good one be born among my descendants?”
sentences.n: Töreġešü is töre- ‘be born’ + -ġešü, the front-vowel conditional (Ming 生呵). Nigen-üġü is ‘one’ + -üġü (Ming 一箇也 ‘even one’), perhaps the same question particle as in Žüči-(j)üġü in §254; törekü ažuγ̇u (Ming 生麽 有來) is the participle + ‘there was’. I take it as a rhetorical question that expects ‘one good one will be born’; the reverse reading, ‘not even one good one will be born’, cannot be ruled out. The quotation closes at ažuγ̇u".

morph.gloss: I (first-person singular pronoun; stem min- before case endings) [我的]
particle (the Ming 也 'even'; compare the question -üġü)

sentences.i: so he said, and the decree was issued.
sentences.n: Boluγ̇ad is bol- + the linking vowel + the converb -γ̇ad, ‘having become’, the converb closing §255; there is no finite verb, and I give the Ming’s 做了 (‘done’) as the sense. Keġen ‘saying’ is the tag of the last quotation.

sentences.t: Čiṅgis Qaγan morilarun Taṅγ̇ud irgen-ü Burqan-dur elčin ilerün:
sentences.l: Chinggis Qaγan when-mounting, Tangut people-of Burqan-to envoy when-sending:
sentences.i: When Chinggis Qahan mounted to ride out, he sent an envoy to Burqan of the Tangut people, saying:
sentences.n: Two converbs of time in -run / -rün: morilarun (mori ‘horse’ + -la- ‘ride’ + -run, Ming 上馬時 ‘when mounting’) and ilerün (ile- ‘send’, Ming 差時, ‘when sending’). Burqan is a man’s name here (Ming 人名), not the holy mountain. Irgen-ü is the genitive -ü after n, ‘the people’s’. The message begins with the next unit.

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]
the Tangut, a people (plural in -d) [種(名)]
Burqan, a man's name [人名 行]

sentences.i: “‘Let me be your right hand,’ you said.
sentences.n: Bolsu is bol- ‘be’ + the optative -su (Ming 做我, ‘let me be’); keġelüġe is keġe- ‘say’ + -lüġe, the past ‘had said’ (Ming 說來), with no person marked, hence the reminder ‘you said’. The message opens at Baraγ̇un (Shiratori’s mark) and closes at morila". The inner single quotes are mine.

sentences.t: či. Sartaγ̇ul irgen-e altan arγamži-jan tasuldažu ölülčen morilaba.
sentences.l: You Sartaul people-to golden leash-own being-cut, confronting, mounted.
sentences.i: As for you, the Sartaul people’s golden leash having been cut, I mounted to settle it.
sentences.n: A hard sentence, given as a reading. Altan is here Ming 金 ‘gold’ and Shiratori prints it in lower case, against the capital in §254, so ‘golden leash’; the parallel altan žiloγ̇a ‘golden breast-strap’ later in this § points the same way (an item of harness). Tasuldažu is tasul- ‘cut off’ + passive -da- + -žu (Ming 被斷着, ‘being cut’); ölülčen (Ming 折證) has a stem ölülče- I infer, ‘to settle by confrontation’, and is uncertain. Who mounted (‘I’ is my reading from §254) and whom the leash bound are open questions.

morph.gloss: the Sartaul, a people (the Ming 囘囘 'Muslims') [囘囘]
leash, leading-rope (Ming 縻繩) [縻繩 自的行]
to settle by confrontation, bear witness (stem inferred from the Ming 折證) [折證]

sentences.t: bi. Baraγ̇un γar bolun morila" keġežü ileġesü
sentences.l: I right hand being, mount" saying, if-sending,
sentences.i: ‘I, being the right hand, mount!’ saying so, when the envoy went,
sentences.n: The envoy’s words, quoted in a message already in quotes. Bi here is ‘I’ (Ming 我), not ‘is’; bolun is the converb ‘being’; morila is the bare stem ‘mount!’. Ileġesü (ile- ‘send’ + conditional -ġesü, Ming 去呵) is ‘when (the envoy) went’, but the subject is a reading from the context. The message closes at morila".

morph.gloss: I (first-person singular pronoun; stems na-, nama-, min- before case endings) [我]
verb-maker: to ride (the bare stem, used as imperative: mount!)

sentences.t: Burqan-(n)i doṅγoduγ̇ai üdüġüj-e urida Ašaγambu ügülerün:
sentences.l: Burqan-(acc) not-yet-sounding first Asha Gambu saying:
sentences.i: Before Burqan had made a sound, Asha Gambu spoke up first:
sentences.n: Burqan-(n)i has the accusative, ‘Burqan’ as the one who has not yet sounded. Doṅγoduγai (Ming 作聲, ‘make a noise’) has an ending I cannot fully name; üdüġüj-e (Ming 未, ‘not yet’) gives ‘before’. Urida ‘first’. Asha Gambu is Ašaγambu in the print, a man’s name (Ming 人名), spelled in the house way, as with Jaqa Gambu.

morph.gloss: to sound, make a noise [作聲]
ending uncertain ('not yet sounding' with üdüġüj-e)
Asha Gambu, a man's name [人名]
converb of time: saying, when saying

sentences.i: “While he has no strength, what is it to become a qan?”
sentences.n: Jadan böġetele is jada- ‘be unable’ + -n and bü- ‘be’ + -tele ‘while’ (Ming 有間); qān boltala is qān + bol- ‘become’ + -tala ‘until’ (Ming 皇帝做). Küčü is the bare noun ‘strength’. Who lacks the strength — Burqan or Chinggis — and what exactly Asha Gambu means by the question is not clear from the Ming; I take it as an insult to the Qan, which is why the Tangut then sent back ‘great words’. The quotation opens at Küčü and closes at jaγ̇un".

morph.gloss: to be (böġe- before an ending) [有間]
ruler, sovereign, khan (title; the short form beside qaγan) [皇帝]

sentences.t: keġežü čerig ülü nemen jeke üge ügüležü iležüġü.
sentences.l: Saying, soldiers not adding, great word speaking, sent.
sentences.i: So saying, they added no soldiers, spoke big words, and sent them.
sentences.n: Keġežü, ügüležü are converbs in -žü, the chain’s verb being iležüġü (ile- ‘send’ + past narrative -žüġü, Ming 敎來了). Nemen is a converb of neme- ‘add’ (Ming 添), negated by ülü. The subject (the Tangut, as I take it) and what was sent are not stated: ‘big words’ (jeke üge, Ming 大話) may be the object of sent. See the earlier note on ile- ‘send’ against 去 ‘go’.

sentences.i: Then Chinggis Qahan said:
sentences.n: Tende ‘there, then’ (Ming 那裏), the opening of the reply. The speech runs on to teli" in the last unit of the §.

morph.gloss: there, then (from tere 'that'; locative adverb) [那裏]
Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]
converb of time: saying, when saying

sentences.i: “‘How was it that Asha Gambu spoke so?’ I said.
sentences.n: Ašaγambu-da has the dative-locative -da, which in a passive names the doer (compare Teṅgeri-de, ‘by Heaven’, below); ügülegden is ügüle- + passive -gde- + -n; büleġei is bü- ‘be’ + the past -leġei (Ming 有來), ‘used to be’. The ‘by Asha Gambu’ is therefore a reading; ‘to Asha Gambu’ is the other. Shiratori prints no closing mark at keġen; the Qan’s speech runs on to teli", and the single quotes in `i` mark only this inner thought.

morph.gloss: Asha Gambu, a man's name [人名 行]
dative-locative: to, by (the doer of a passive; uncertain)
past: there was, used to be (Ming 來)

sentences.t: araγača an-dur böġed kelbes žorižü ileġesü jaγ̇un berketü büleġei.
sentences.l: By-reckoning them-to then turning aiming, if-going, what difficult used-to-be.
sentences.i: Reckoning it up, had I turned on them and gone against them, what would have been hard?
sentences.n: Araγača (Ming 論來, 計量 ‘by reckoning’), an-dur (‘to them’, the stem an- + -dur), and a chain of converbs: kelbes (Ming 翻着, ‘turning’; a stem kelbe- I infer) and žorižü (‘aiming’) leading to ileġesü ‘if going’. Jaγ̇un berketü büleġei is ‘what difficulty (berke ‘hard’ + -tü ‘having’; the possessive -tü type) there was’. The conditional ‘had I’ is mine; the Mongol has no person.

morph.gloss: as for, going by (Ming 論來, 計量 'reckoning'; form unclear) [計量]
they, them (third-person stem before case endings) [他每 行]
converb ending (uncertain): being so, and then
to turn over, turn about (stem inferred from the Ming 翻) [翻着]
to aim at, set out for [指着]

sentences.t: Öġere maqa küġün-dür žorižü büküi-dür-že teli.
sentences.l: Otherwise perhaps man-to aiming, at-the-being indeed, that-matter.
sentences.i: Otherwise, perhaps, aiming at a man — as matters stand, leave that matter.
sentences.n: Hard, and given as a reading. Öġere is ‘other, apart’ (Ming 𠮠); maqa ‘perhaps’; büküi-dür-že is bü- ‘be’ + participle -küi + dative-locative -dür + -že (Ming 有時 且罷, where 且罷 ‘let it be, for now’ is the clue). Teli (Ming 那事) is ‘that matter’; the word is uncertain. Chinggis seems to say that he could settle with the Tangut but will not now.

sentences.t: Müṅke teṅgeri-de igeġegdeġesü altan žiloγ̇a batuda tatažu ireġesü
sentences.l: Eternal Heaven-by, if-helped, golden breast-strap firmly pulling, if-coming,
sentences.i: If Eternal Heaven helps me, and I come back pulling the golden breast-strap tight,
sentences.n: Igeġegdeġesü is igeġe- ‘protect, help’ (a stem inferred from the Ming 護助) + passive -gde- + conditional -ġesü; teṅgeri-de is ‘by Heaven’, the dative-locative naming the doer. Müṅke teṅgeri (Ming 長生天) is ‘Eternal Heaven’. Žiloγ̇a (Ming 牽胷 ‘pull-breast’) is a piece of harness and the sense ‘breast-strap’ is a guess; tatažu is ‘pulling’ (the Ming 扯着) and batuda ‘firmly’ (batu + -da). The image is of a firm return, as I read it.

sentences.i: then there, perhaps, let that matter be done,” saying so,
sentences.n: Boltuγai is bol- + the optative -tuγai (Ming 做者, ‘let it be done’), with maqa (Ming 莫不) ‘perhaps’. The speech closes at teli", and keġežü ‘saying’ ends the § on a converb, with the sentence running on into the next §.
